1.note: Literally "raising smoke": read as smoking tobacco (pipes), usual at such Dutch gatherings. The phrase also echoes the incense of the Temple, perhaps with irony.

2.note: Literally "the five kinds". Not the five species of grain here; probably the five kinds of funds or collections for the Land of Israel that an emissary explained to donors. Sense uncertain.

3.note: Spanish/Portuguese padrinos, "patrons, godfathers": the members of the Portuguese community appointed to sponsor and organize the emissary's collection. In paragraph 95 they are Aaron Capadose and Moses de Isaac Suasso.

4.note: "On 3 Nisan, at night". By Hebrew reckoning the night of 3 Nisan is the evening of Monday 30 March; if the Ḥida means the night after the day of 3 Nisan, it is the evening of Tuesday 31 March. The same applies to "14 Iyyar, at night" in paragraph 96 (the evening of Sunday 10 May or of Monday 11 May).

5.note: R. Saul Lowenstamm (1717–1790), chief rabbi of the Ashkenazi community of Amsterdam from 1755; called "the head of the Ashkenazi rabbinic court" in paragraph 96 and "our teacher R. Saul" (מוהר"ש) elsewhere.

6.note: R. Solomon Shalem (Salem), ḥakham of the Portuguese (Sephardi) community of Amsterdam; he had earlier lived and served in Belgrade (paragraph 93).

7.note: Literally "had it been [the reading] Beshallaḥ", that is, had he said this some two months earlier (the Sabbath of Beshallaḥ was 7 February 1778), near the start of the Ḥida's stay, when it could still have helped the collection.

8.note: So printed: "I did not speak that night". Perhaps he did not expound the Haggadah at length as usual; sense uncertain.

9.note: Probably Spanish silla (de manos) or Italian sedia, a sedan chair.

10.note: Read as Spanish/Portuguese acciones/acções, "shares" (Dutch actiën), on which Amsterdam merchants speculated; the spelling is closer to ocasiones, "occasions, chances" (unlucky ventures). Sense probable, not certain. The florin is the Dutch guilder.

11.note: Read as the Sephardi family name Gutierrez (Gutiérrez).

12.note: The Ḥida uses the formula for removing leaven before Passover: it is enough to "nullify it in one's heart" [b. Pesaḥim 4b]. The man "nullified" his Passover invitation in the same way, without a word.

13.note: The Ḥida's attendant on the journey. Probably the same "Abraham" whom he sent on an errand in part 2; not identified further.

14.note: Printed אזיזידו here and אזוידו a few lines below; read as the Portuguese name Azevedo, a well-known family of the Amsterdam community.

15.he: ייא פת"אח ייא רזאק ייא כארים
15.note: Arabic yā Fattāḥ, yā Razzāq, yā Karīm, "O Opener, O Provider, O Generous One", names of God called out in the streets.

16.note: So printed (checked on the scan). Read as "Arabistan" (ערביסטאן, the land of the Arabs, with מ for ט). A reading "in Ramadan" does not fit the letters.

17.note: Bolechów (Bolekhiv) in eastern Galicia. Not identified further; from the context he came with R. Saul and his son, perhaps one of R. Saul's circle.

18.note: R. Abraham Joshua Heschel of Kraków (about 1595–1663), the great Polish talmudist, who left almost no written work; the second story explains why.

19.note: R. Shabbetai Sheftel Horowitz (about 1590–1660), son of R. Isaiah Horowitz, author of the Shelah (Shenei Luḥot ha-Berit), and author of Vavei ha-Amudim. He became rabbi of Vienna only in 1655, so the year [5]408 [1648] does not fit; the story is as told.

20.note: Literally "did not find his hands" (compare b. Bava Batra 10a, "did not find his hands and feet"): he could not find his way through it.

21.note: Abbreviation read as Aramaic be-hai gavna, "in the same way". Not certain.

22.note: A merchant's name in Hebrew letters. Perhaps the Dutch surname van den Ende, with ו for "van"; this is a suggestion only, not checked in the Amsterdam records.

23.note: So printed; read as בסוף הבית, "at the end of the room". Perhaps he sat apart because the women were playing cards.

24.note: The Mahamad, the board of wardens that governed the Portuguese Jewish community of Amsterdam.

25.note: Printed with an abbreviation mark. Read as "the fathers" (האבות), perhaps the padrinos ("godfathers"); possibly an abbreviation not resolved.

26.note: Aramaic: "that a sign rested", with a play on נחית, "You led", the first word of the verse: the two padrinos were named Moses and Aaron.

27.note: "Who was their emissary": R. A. Ze'evi had collected from the Ashkenazim shortly before, so a second gift so soon was unexpected. He appears with the Ḥida in Amsterdam in part 6.

28.note: So printed (checked on the scan). 29 Iyyar 5538 was Tuesday 26 May 1778, the day after he left Amsterdam (paragraph 100: Monday of the week of Bamidbar, 25 May); and the next entry is the Sabbath of Behar, 23 May. Probably a misprint for 21 Iyyar (כ"א, the evening of Monday 18 May) or 19 Iyyar (י"ט, the evening of Saturday 16 May); "from Tuesday" would then be 19 May.

29.note: Hebrew yiḥus ("pedigree, the distinguished") with Spanish de la Nación: the leading families of the Portuguese "Nation" of Amsterdam.

30.note: Literally "to give them graces": probably a calque of Spanish dar las gracias, "to give thanks"; a farewell visit of thanks.

31.note: "The ship": from Amsterdam to The Hague this was probably the canal passenger boat (trekschuit), not a sea-going ship.

32.note: Read as Portuguese Haia, "The Hague". Part 8 opens on the New Moon of Sivan "in the city of איוא", with Tobias Boaz, a leading Jew of The Hague.
